neutral_definition_context.state: State abbreviates EuclideanSpace ℝ ι for a finite index type ι.
neutral_definition_context.rn_log_ratio: RNLogRatio.logRatio mu pi is definitionally MeasureTheory.llr mu pi: x ↦ Real.log ((mu.rnDeriv pi x).toReal). The RN representative is the existing Mathlib choice; real logarithm and ENNReal.toReal are total functions.
neutral_definition_context.gradient: gradient phi x is the Riesz inverse of Mathlib's total fderiv. At nondifferentiability points the total derivative/gradient has the canonical default zero. MeasurableGradient.measurable_gradient proves measurability of this total map.
neutral_definition_context.smooth_finite_domain: SmoothFiniteScoreDomain mu pi has three fields: mu ≪ pi; mu-a.e. DifferentiableAt ℝ (RNLogRatio.logRatio mu pi); and Integrable (fun x => norm(gradient(logRatio mu pi) x)^2) mu.
neutral_definition_context.information: CanonicalRelativeFisher.information mu pi h is RelativeFisher.information with base mu, density constant one and logRatio mu pi; by the existing theorem it equals the real Bochner integral of the squared gradient norm under mu. Its domain witness prevents treating a nonintegrable squared score as finite via total-integral conventions.
neutral_definition_context.coupling: Transport.IsCoupling gamma mu nu is gamma.fst = mu ∧ gamma.snd = nu. It does not itself assert probability normalization or finite total mass.
neutral_definition_context.optimal_coupling: DisplacementInterpolation.IsQuadraticOptimalCoupling adds that the ENNReal lintegral of quadraticCost under gamma equals Transport.transportCost quadraticCost mu nu.
neutral_definition_context.wasserstein: quadraticCost(x,y) = ENNReal.ofReal(norm(x-y)^2). transportCost is the ENNReal infimum of all coupling costs. wassersteinDistance mu nu is its ENNReal rpow 1/2. The leaf returns its ENNReal.toReal value. Existing finite optimal cost identity plus a focused test proves this distance is not infinity under the leaf's assumptions.
neutral_definition_context.analytic_vs_interpretive_fields: The pure L2 estimate uses squared-score integrability, total-gradient measurability, coupling marginal identities, and moments. Absolute continuity and a.e. differentiability remain inside the inherited domain guard; they are not established from textbook density prose. They alone do not identify an arbitrary chosen RN gradient with a weak/Sobolev Wasserstein gradient.
